To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the presence of CK-only-positive sentinel nodes is associated with a high rate of subsequent metastases.
the presence of CK-only-positive SNs was not significantly associated with subsequent metastases in patients who were node-negative by HE staining.
the association of CK-only-positive SLNs and subsequent metastases is not significant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new and more effective methods for the diagnosis of cancer.
the association of cytokeratins (CK)-only-positive SLNs (SLN+) and the subsequent metastases in BC.
the development of new and efficient algorithms for the detection, classification, and segmentation of objects in medical imaging.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of CK-only-positive sentinel nodes is associated with subsequent metastases.

the presence of a CK-only-positive SLN in a patient without a clinically suspicious axilla is not associated with increased risk of subsequent metastases in the axilla and is thus not a contraindication for breast-conserving treatment.
the use of the CK20 antibody is a valuable adjunct in sentinel node evaluation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the association of cytokeratins only-positive sentinel nodes (CK-SNs) and subsequent metastases is unclear.
a cytokeratin-positive solitary node is not associated with subsequent nodal or distant recurrence, even when the sentinel node is the only involved lymph node.
the presence of CK+ SNs in patients with negative IHC SNs is associated with subsequent metastasis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of cytokeratin (CK)-only positive sentinel lymph nodes (SLNs) is associated with subsequent axillary metastases.
the cytokeratin-only positive sentinel lymph nodes should be considered as metastasis and the patient should be treated as such.
the presence of CK-positive SNLs in breast cancer patients is associated with a significantly higher risk of distant metastases.
